title: What Would You Trust AI to Do for You?
paragraphs: Asking AI to help write an email is one thing. Handing it your money and saying, "Go shopping"? That might take a little more trust.
A global survey of 11,000 people by Talker Research looked at where people draw the line when it comes to trusting AI.
It found that 66% were comfortable using AI in their personal lives and at work. And on average, respondents said they knowingly used AI around six times a week.

They were most comfortable using it for general learning, such as finding out about a hobby or learning what a book is about. They also felt comfortable using it for DIY projects, writing emails and creating pictures for fun.
But what about letting AI make decisions on its own?
Just 31% of respondents said they were likely to trust it to do this — for example, by choosing things to buy or making appointments for them. That figure was highest in India, at 70%!
Across the survey, respondents said they would let AI spend an average of $200 to buy something without checking with them first.
When it came to dealing with companies, people wanted to know if AI was involved. For 56%, this was more important than getting the fastest, most accurate result.
If respondents thought a company was using AI without telling them, 39% would be more careful about sharing personal information. One in five said they would leave its website immediately.
AI did not always act in a trustworthy way, either. In fact, 40% had caught it giving wrong or made-up information at least once.
Even so, 43% said they trusted AI more than they did a year ago.
